Number of food recalls normal, but outbreaks worse, says MN Dept. of Agriculture

By WDIO
September 14, 2026 - 6:16 PM
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:15
Instaread

Food recalls have been in the news a lot lately, and the state has a multi-tiered system to stop them from reaching your plate.

Alida Sorenson works in food and feed safety at the Minnesota Department of Agriculture. She said there don’t seem to be more food recalls than normal this year, despite heavy media attention. However, the severity of outbreaks related to contaminated food are much worse, like the recent salmonella outbreak on jalapeños and the cyclospora outbreak on lettuce.

Cyclospora didn’t hit Minnesota hard, Sorenson said, but the public health system has a plan when dangerous items hit the shelves.

“We have inspectors who are up there in the Northwoods, up in Duluth,” she said. “And they would go out to all of those grocery stores or locations where those food items might have gone to make sure that they’ve been pulled from the shelves.”

Bigger box stores sometimes stop you from scanning recalled products altogether, she said. Fortunately, outbreaks have slowed down as we reach the end of summer, but you can make sure you haven’t purchased anything unsafe by checking the MN Dept. of Ag’s weekly food recall newsletter.
